findings.claim: The device_notes plague digit is false and internally inconsistent: the psalm's catalogue represents 8 of the traditional ten plagues, not 7, and 7 covered plus 2 omitted cannot total ten.
findings.grounds: device_notes states the sequence '(darkness, blood, frogs, insects, hail, locusts, and the death of the firstborn) covers 7 of the traditional plagues and omits the livestock-pestilence and boils'. From the bytes of 105:28-36 the catalogue names eight distinct plague objects, because 105:31 carries TWO nouns - 'עָרֹ֑ב' and 'כִּ֝נִּ֗ים' - which the sibling row M8-Ps-341 counts separately in its own observed_substrate_signals ('105:31 carries two nouns (arov, kinnim)'); collapsing them into the single word 'insects' is what produces the 7. With exactly two omissions named the arithmetic must close at ten, so 7 is one short on the row's own terms. The count OBJECT is also unnamed and out of scope: 'the traditional plagues' is an Exodus-scoped set that the Ps-scoped staged tools cannot sweep - the section 11 OL-c28 class, where a claim must be scoped explicitly or dropped. The trailing clause 'omits the livestock-pestilence and boils material present in this psalm's own catalogue by their absence' is self-contradictory as written. Not load-bearing: device_notes itself labels the observation 'texture, not boundary authority for these rows', and neither of the row's seams rests on it.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only, no span effect. Either scope the count to the psalm's own bytes with its object named - for example 'the catalogue names 8 distinct plague objects across 105:28-36, two of them (arov, kinnim) inside 105:31' - or drop the cross-book comparison the Ps-scoped tools cannot verify. Rewrite the self-contradictory trailing clause.

findings.claim: The 105:31|32 seam rests on a content grouping the row itself concedes is not a grammatical break, while the row's own byte evidence names a stronger rival seam at 105:32|33 and a repeated verse-opening formula that the seam cuts apart.

Verse-opening tokens MT 105:25-37: 105:25 'הָפַ֣ךְ', 105:26 'שָׁ֭לַח', 105:27 'שָֽׂמוּ', 105:28 'שָׁ֣לַֽח', 105:29, 105:30, 105:31 'אָ֭מַר וַיָּבֹ֣א' and 105:32 'נָתַ֣ן' are ALL waw-less; 105:33 'וַיַּ֣ךְ' is the first waw-initial opener; 105:34 'אָ֭מַר וַיָּבֹ֣א' is waw-less again; 105:35 and 105:36 'וַיַּ֣ךְ' are waw-initial. So (a) the shipped seam 105:31|32 falls INSIDE an unbroken run of waw-less 3ms perfect openers - the row concedes exactly this in its own observed_substrate_signals ('the split stands only as a content grouping, not a grammatical break') and names 105:32|33 'the byte-true rival seam'; (b) the row also discloses that the two-word opener 'אָ֭מַר וַיָּבֹ֣א' recurs BYTE-identically at oshb:Ps.105.31 and oshb:Ps.105.34 (re-collated here: byte tier at both refs), a repeated verse-opening formula whose two members the shipped seam separates into different rows while reading it only as a 'continuity signal'; taken as a group-opener it would seam at 105:30|31 and 105:33|34. (c) No section 5 tier-1 internal-seam class (superscription, hallelu-Yah/hodu frame, doxology, acrostic, explicit speaker/addressee shift) stands at 105:31|32, and section 6 requires strophe rows at tier-1-supported internal seams; by contrast the seam this pair holds at 105:27|28 IS byte-supported, by a 3mp-to-3ms subject shift ('שָֽׂמוּ', Moses and Aaron, to 'שָׁ֣לַֽח', YHWH), which 105:31|32 lacks. The defect is choosing the weaker of two byte-visible options the row itself lays out, not a byte-false statement: every Hebrew run in the row collates BYTE at its cited ref and all of its WEB quotations are verbatim.
findings.proposed_change: Seam-pair proposal - ONE cure installed on BOTH M8-Ps-341 and M8-Ps-342 per the section 10 seam-pair rule; routed onward, not adjudicated here. findings.claim: The prose label 'the mizmor-shir-le-David title' reverses the word order of the title it quotes in the same clause.
findings.grounds: oshb:Ps.108.1 reads 'שִׁ֖יר מִזְמ֣וֹר לְדָוִֽד' - 'שִׁ֖יר' first, 'מִזְמ֣וֹר' second (spliced from verse_map_oshb.json; the run collates BYTE at oshb:Ps.108.1). Section 2a treats these label classes as byte-swept memberships and shir-mizmor against mizmor-shir is a distinguishable title order, so naming it 'mizmor-shir' mis-glosses the quoted run. Quote/gloss parity only, not load-bearing: the title is tier-1 opener evidence whatever its internal order, the dual-cite web:Ps.108.0 = oshb:Ps.108.1 required of a titled psalm's opening row by the section 1 owner gate is present and arithmetically correct, and the row's seam at 108:5|108:6 matches the section 11 p26 erratum's byte-verified join exactly (Ps 108 = Ps 57:7-11 + Ps 60:5-12, joining at WEB 108:5|108:6 = MT 108:6|108:7), which is why high confidence survives.
